title: flow-conserving admission scheduler with deadline windows for dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets currently use token-bucket and priority-lane strategies that can either over-reserve capacity for low-utilization tenants or aggressively shed too many requests during short bursts, causing missed soft SLOs for premium customers. We need an admission controller that preserves aggregate flow (minimizes wasted tokens), honors tenant-level soft deadlines, and cooperates with autoscaler signals to maintain throughput guarantees without oscillation.

Proposal: Implement a flow-conserving admission scheduler that operates at the fleet ingress. Key concepts: 1) Deadline windows: each request can carry a deadline tier (now, <100ms, <300ms, >300ms) inferred from route or token metadata. 2) Conserved tokens: admission tokens are reserved for the duration of queue wait across batching boundaries so scheduling is aware of actual in-flight capacity. 3) Elastic soft guarantees: tenants with reserved throughput receive weighted admission shares, but unused share can be shared across tenants within a short reclaim window to improve utilization. 4) Autoscaler handshake: scheduler exposes a backlog and headroom signal to autoscaler to avoid reactive scale-ups/downs during transient bursts.

Scope: fleet-level admission and short-queueing (sub-second). Does not change long-term throttles applied at the API edge. Integrations: Dedicated routing layer, per-tenant quotas, autoscaler metrics endpoint, Console dashboards for per-tenant admission stats.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler admits requests respecting weighted throughput shares for reserved tenants under sustained load
Deadline windows achieve 95% on-time responses for 'now' tier and >=90% for '<100ms' tier under synthetic burst tests up to 1.5x provisioned throughput
Idle reserved capacity is reclaimed within 250ms and reallocated to other tenants without violating guarantees
Autoscaler uses published backlog/headroom signals to avoid >2x scale oscillation within a 5-minute window during step loads
Integration tests and perf benchmarks added to CI with guardrails to prevent regressions
design_notes: Admission queue is implemented as per-node prioritized FIFO with per-tenant subqueues. A global admission loop allocates tokens every 10ms slice.

Conservation model: when a token is allocated to a request that then waits for batching/kv cache, the token stays marked until the request is either started on GPU or evicted by admission. This prevents double-counting of headroom.
Deadline tiers are annotated by client SDK when possible and inferred in the routing layer using route metadata and recent p95 latencies for that route.
Weight sharing uses a short reclaim window (configurable default 250ms) to let unused reserved capacity flow to other queues but reclaims it quickly when owner tenant resumes.
Expose metrics: per-tenant admitted rate, blocked rate, drop rate, deadline-miss-rate, reclaimed-share, backlog-size, headroom-estimate. Add traces for decision paths to Console.
Edge cases: long-tail batching (very large batch waits) will be capped to avoid token hoarding; very small tenants may be grouped into a best-effort pool to reduce scheduling overhead.
rollout_plan: Week 1 (canary): deploy scheduler as opt-in on two small dedicated pools with synthetic traffic and low-stakes tenants
Week 2 (observability): collect metrics and dashboard; run automated SLO regression tests; iterate on reclaim window and slice size
Week 3 (wider canary): enable for a subset of medium fleets and expose autoscaler handshake signals to the autoscaler in read-only mode
Week 4 (guarded rollout): enable autoscaler handshake in read-write mode; gradually increase tenant coverage by 25% per day while monitoring p95/p99 and scale oscillations
Rollback: feature flag to revert to existing admission; warm-up cache for token accounting disabled on rollback to avoid residual state
test_plan: Unit tests for token conservation logic and per-tenant weight math
Integration tests with autoscaler mock to validate handshake semantics
Perf harness: replay real customer traces plus synthetic burst profiles (step/impulse/sine) against canary pools
Chaos test: simulate node loss and verify graceful shedding and bounded SLA impact
E2E smoke: verify Console dashboards and alerting fire for configured thresholds
